rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous person returns to his paradisal family willingly and joyfully, recognizing them and the rank prepared for him as he knew them in worldly life.
rows.anchor: يرجع من نفسه من غير مزعج برغبة وقبول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive wording of ‘joyful’ depicts unqualified happiness; he receives a garden and silk after worldly anxiety, self-examination, hardship, and distress.
rows.anchor: أي قد أوتي جنة وحريرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aisha questioned how the hadith that everyone examined perishes could fit the verse saying that some receive their book in the right hand.
rows.anchor: أحدهما ( ليس أحد يحاسب إلا هلك ) والثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the first wording was what Aisha heard, the contradiction is explicit; if the second was heard, its wording may reflect a narrator’s alteration.
rows.anchor: إن كان اللفظ الأول هو الذي سمعته فالإشكال فيه واضح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aisha knew that the record contains every deed, including small and great ones, so the verse’s promise still appeared to conflict with exhaustive reckoning.
rows.anchor: والصديقة رضي الله عنها عالمة بأن الكتاب يثبت فيه جميع الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith uses accounting in its full sense: listing every deed and requiting each; the verse uses the whole term for only the listing, without requital.
rows.anchor: وأن المراد بالحساب في الآية جزء المعنى المطابقي

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha explained that the believer is reminded of his sins and then they are passed over, as Abu Hayyan transmits from her.
rows.anchor: يقرر بذنوبه ثم يتجاوز عنها

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: A report in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections says God covers the believer, makes him acknowledge his sins, then says He concealed them in life and forgives them today.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word kanf means a bird’s wing, an image of the utmost tenderness with which God treats the believer.
rows.anchor: فإن كنفه الطائر جناحه , وهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned receive their record in the left hand, with the whole rear direction signifying evil because they acted as though God could not see them.
rows.anchor: أي في شماله إيتاء مستغرقا لجميع جهة الوراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hand placement fits a right hand bound to the neck and the left brought behind the back, contrasting the saved person’s gesture of affection with the damned person’s treachery.
rows.anchor: فكان حقيقا بأن تعل يمينه إلى عنقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thubūr means regret and ruin encompassing every kind of misery, fitting deeds characteristic of the doomed.
rows.anchor: أي حسرة وندما بنحو قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sinner is immersed in intensely blazing fire and surrounded by its heat because he followed desires already encircled by fire.
rows.anchor: ويغمس في النار التي هي في غاية الاتقاد ويقاسي حرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His worldly pleasure among his family was arrogant attachment to wealth and status, offered as a warning that should draw people toward repentance.
rows.anchor: استعطافا إلى التوبة وتحذيرا من السرور في دار الحزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly complacent person does not grieve for sins or wrongdoing; instead, he is pleased by them and faces a hard reckoning and sorrowful return.
rows.anchor: لا يحزن أحدهم لذنب عمله ولا لقبيح ارتكبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage uses interlocking omission: easy reckoning, the result, first implies its opposite later, while family joy, the later cause, implies earlier grief and self-accounting.
rows.anchor: ذكر الحساب اليسير الذي هو الثمرة والمسبب أولا يدل على حذف ضده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥāra can mean to return to one’s Lord, diminish, or perish; the denial echoes those who say life is only worldly and time destroys them.
rows.anchor: أي يرجع إلى ربه أو ينقص أو لهلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bala affirms that the denier will surely return humbled, diminished, and ruined.
rows.anchor: ليرجعن صاغرا ناقصا هالكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God saw the condemned person at his first creation and knows all his deeds, so leaving him unaccountable would contradict wisdom, justice, and sovereignty.
rows.anchor: في إعادته كما كان في ابتدائه وفي جميع أعماله وأحواله التي لا يجوز في عدل عادل ترك الحساب عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After evidence for resurrection, the oath reassures the denier; leaving an oath over an even clearer claim invites reflection and is more eloquent than swearing explicitly.
rows.anchor: وترك الحلف على ما هو ظاهر أبلغ من الحلف لما في ذلك الترك من تنبيه المخاطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shafaq is the western twilight after sunset, passing from red through yellow and murky white to darkness; its name suggests delicacy, as in tenderness of heart.
rows.anchor: الضياء الذي يكون في المغرب عقب غروب الشمس أطباقا حمرة ثم صفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night overcomes and removes twilight; what it gathers includes everything in its darkness, such as twilight, the preceding day, and stars, evidencing its Creator’s power to originate and resurrect.
rows.anchor: جمع في بطنه وطرد وساق من ذلك الشفق ومن النهار الذي كان قبله والنجوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon’s phases, from disappearance through a thin crescent to fullness and waning, make its cycle an evident sign that its Maker can restore what has vanished.
rows.anchor: انتظم واستوى واجتمع كماله وتم أمره ليلة إبداره بعد أن كان قد غاب أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These immense signs and benefits demonstrate God’s complete power to restore things exactly as they were; the resurrection claim is so evident that it needs no supporting oath.
rows.anchor: كل منها مع ذلك دال على تمام قدرته تعالى على الذي يراد تقريره في العقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read laturkabunna with a damma on bāʾ, implying deletion of the plural wāw; Ibn Kathir, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi read it with fatḥa, addressing the human as a singular by form.
rows.anchor: على قراءة الجماعة بضم الباء دلالة على حذف واو الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭabaqan ʿan ṭabaq means one state after another through life, death, barzakh, resurrection, gathering, accounting, the scale, the path, and final abode; moral states also vary in stages.
rows.anchor: حالا بعد حال من أطوار الحياة وأدوار العيش وغمرات الموت ثم من أمور البرزخ وشؤون البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The successive stages are like matching covers or layers; examples include embryo, infant, child, youth, adult, elder, death, resurrection, gathering, reckoning, weighing, crossing, and destination.
rows.anchor: فأول أطباق الإنسان جنين , ثم وليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Changing human states show that people are governed by another; whoever understands this sees that the will directing affairs belongs to God, not the self.
rows.anchor: من كان اليوم على حالة وغدا على أخرى جدير بأن يعلم أن تدبيره إلى سواه

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
rows.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq names changing conditions, weakened power and limbs, and the force of divine will as proofs of the Creator.
rows.anchor: لأبي بكر الوراق : ما الدليل على الصانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not prostrating before the Quran means refusing inward humility and submission to truth, and therefore also refusing the ritual prostration required when it is recited.
rows.anchor: أي يخضعون بالقلب ويتذللون للحق بالسجود اللغوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran contains comprehensive worldly and afterlife benefits, distinguishes lawful from unlawful, and bears self-evident testimony to its divine origin and miraculousness.
rows.anchor: الجامع لكل ما ينفعهم في دنياهم وأخراهم الفارق بين كل ملتبس من الحرام والحلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the rhetorical question implies that they have no excuse, bal shifts from an implied subject to the explicit description ‘those who disbelieve,’ naming what drives their denial.
rows.anchor: وضع الظاهر موضع المضمر تعميما وتنبيها على الوصف الذي حملهم على التكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the disbelief and enmity stored in their hearts, fed by distracting lusts such as love of leadership and claims to divinity.
rows.anchor: يضعون في أوعية صدورهم من الكفر والعداوة بسبب الشهوات الشاغلة لهم وهي حب الرئاسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the painful punishment glad tidings is deliberate irony: if they are ever to receive good news, it is this threat.
rows.anchor: أي أخبرهم يا أفضل الخلق وأكملهم وأعدلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief is confession and righteous deeds demonstrate its truth; their reward is God’s great bounty, including pardon and concealment of minor sins, never ending, diminishing, or reproachful.
rows.anchor: أي عظيم وثواب جزيل يعلمه الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deeds do not truly cause the reward, which rests on enveloping mercy; omission of the causal fa signals this, unlike the context of Surat al-Tin.
rows.anchor: أسقط الفاء المؤذنة بالسبب تنبيها على ذلك بخلاف ما في سورة التين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose of Surat al-Buruj is to show God’s power to reward the faithful and punish the wicked, as already stated at the end of Surat al-Inshiqaq; the worldly punishment of persecutors consoles and strengthens believers.
rows.anchor: مقصودها الدلالة على القدرة على مقصود الانشقاق الذي هو صريح آخرها من تنعيم الولي وتعذيب الشقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala calls God merciful to all creatures through justice and forbearance, and especially merciful to His allies by completing their blessing.
rows.anchor: الذي عم الخلائق عدلا وحلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surat al-Fajr argues for return and reckoning, the ending of al-Ghashiya; dawn breaks after the prior day and sleepers rise from the lesser death of sleep to seek livelihood, then face reward or punishment.
rows.anchor: مقصودها الاستدلال على آخر الغاشية الإياب والحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala portrays God as gathering people after their disintegration, granting explanation that prepares whom He wills for faith, and reserving contentment and gardens for His allies.
rows.anchor: جامع العباد بعد تمزيقهم بما له من العظمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conclusion of al-Ghashiya announces return and reckoning; renewed night and day, and Hajj rites performed in pilgrim clothing with talbiya and travel to sacred places, recall resurrection.
rows.anchor: لما ختمت تلك بأنه لا بد من الإياب والحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath’s Fajr is the dawn of the Sacrifice day, when pilgrims enter the sanctuary, leave consecration, and receive God’s hospitality; a new day follows one that has passed without a change in essence.
rows.anchor: وهو فجر يوم النحر الذي هو أول الأيام الآخذة في الإياب إلى بيت الله الحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ten nights are the year’s greatest nights and signify resurrection through people rising to answer God’s call like the dead.
rows.anchor: هي أعظم ليالي العام . وهي آية الله

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr interprets the even as those who complete Hajj in two days and the odd as those who complete it fully.
rows.anchor: أي لمن أتم - قاله ابن الزبير

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Jabir, transmitted by the trustworthy Ayyash ibn ʿUqba and narrated by Ahmad and al-Bazzar with reliable transmitters, identifies the ten as the Adha days, the even as Sacrifice day, and the odd as ʿArafa.
rows.anchor: وروى أحمد والبزار برجال الصحيح عن عياش بن عقبة وهو ثقة عن جابر رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night of departure passes as worldly night passes and dawn replaces its darkness; pilgrims return to their homes after laying down their burdens.
rows.anchor: أي ينقضي كما ينقضي ليل الدنيا وظلام ظلمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Yaʿqub retain the final yāʾ in yasri, while the other readers omit it.
rows.anchor: وأثبت الياء في يسري ابن كثير ويعقوب وحذفها الباقو

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Asked why the final yāʾ was omitted, al-Akhfash answered that night is traveled in rather than itself traveling, so the altered sense requires an altered form; the author says this entails rejecting transmitted affirmation readings.
rows.anchor: فقال : الليل يسرى فيه ولا يسري

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash analogizes the omitted yāʾ in yasri to baghiy, ‘unchaste,’ rather than baghiya, ‘unchaste woman’; the author says this linguistic rationale rejects transmitted readings that affirm the yāʾ.
rows.anchor: عدل لفظه فلم يقل : بغية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Omission may signal pilgrims who remain at the sacred sites, savoring the night, while affirmation may signal those whose full night has passed as they return home at dawn.
rows.anchor: فأشير إلى المجاورين بالحذف حثا على ذلك لما فيه من جلالة المسالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, omission points to a short night and affirmation to a long one, with worshippers standing through the long night before the King.
rows.anchor: فالحذف إشارة إلى القصير والإثبات إشارة إلى الطويل بما وقع من تمام سراه

rows.speaker: تقي الدين بن دقيق العيد
rows.claim: Ibn Daqiq al-ʿId’s verse evokes nights of traveling through the night without sleep or rest, supporting the long-night interpretation.
rows.anchor: كما قال الإمام تقي الدين بن دقيق العيد رحمه الله تعالى حيث قال مشيرا لذلك

rows.speaker: أبو طالب
rows.claim: Abu Talib’s poem invokes the night at Muzdalifah and the stations of Mina as sacred gathering places.
rows.anchor: أبو طالب في قصيدته اللامية المشهورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Differences in night length and in the travelers’ situations show that one sovereign Creator freely controls all these signs and can destroy tyrants.
rows.anchor: فدلت المفاوتة في ذلك وفي جميع أفراد القسم على أن فاعلها قادر مختار واحد قهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥijr means intellect that restrains its owner from desire and raises him toward guidance; anyone whose reason prevents sins and prompts noble conduct possesses it.
rows.anchor: أي عقل فيحجره ويمنعه عن الهوى

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir says that a person who masters and controls himself is described as possessing ḥijr.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جرير : يقال للرجل إذا كان مالكا

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says the oath begins a new reflection: earlier peoples were destroyed after denial and wrongdoing, while God watches every act and hidden thought.
rows.anchor: الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell does not arrive by itself, which might suggest it lies beyond God’s power; angels drag it, and its arrival itself creates overwhelming terror.
rows.anchor: جهنم لا تأتي بنفسها لأنها لو أتت بنفسها لربما ظن أنها خارجة عن القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed report says Hell will be brought with seventy thousand reins, each accompanied by seventy thousand angels.
rows.anchor: روي أنه يؤتى بها لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive wording focuses on the terrifying act of bringing Hell rather than identifying those who bring it; it recalls the verse that Hell is exposed to view.
rows.anchor: وكان المهول نفس المجيء بها لا تعيين الفاعلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated yawm idh clarifies the earlier time marker after a long interruption and magnifies the terror of seeing what awaits the grateful and unbelieving.
rows.anchor: توضيحا لطول الفصل وتهويلا قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity then remembers what helped or harmed in worldly life and sees that attachment to the world brought only loss; remembrance cannot help because the time for action has passed.
rows.anchor: فيعلم أن حبه للدنيا لم يفده إلا خسارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wish that follows is impossible; the person longs to have sent ahead useful striving and deeds.
rows.anchor: أي متمنيا المحال على سبيل التجديد والاستمرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lihayati can mean for the days of worldly life or for this enduring life in which there is no death; the speaker knows obedience had been possible before.
rows.anchor: أي أيام حياتي في الدنيا أو لأجل حياتي هذه الباقية التي لا موت بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one can inflict punishment or restraint like God; with worldly ties severed, no creature’s pain compares with seeing Hell at the gathering, even before entering it.
rows.anchor: لا يقع في خيال أحد لأجل انقطاع الأنساب والأسباب أن أحدا يقدر على مثل ما يقدر عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People in worldly life often imagine human punishment is more severe than God’s, though all worldly torment is less than the terror of seeing Hell there.
rows.anchor: بل يقع في الدنيا في أوهام كثيرة أن عذاب من يخشونه أعظم من عذاب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi and Yaʿqub read both verbs in the passive; the majority read them in the active.
rows.anchor: وبنى الكسائي ويعقوب الفعلين للمفعول

none: The segment contains only an ellipsis in its continuation heading and no commentary text.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surat al-Balad shows that humans lack independent power and that their Creator has it, while divine guidance provides escape from hardship and the path to afterlife happiness; the sanctuary’s provision despite scarcity exemplifies this.
rows.anchor: مقصودها الدلالة على نفي القدرة عن الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala calls God the sole conquering king, whose gifts differ among people and leave each enduring hardship in personal and public concerns, while His allies receive what pleases them and deliverance.
rows.anchor: الذي أسبغ نعمته على سائر بريته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura opens by swearing about the commanding soul, following the tranquil soul and Paradise at the end of al-Fajr; its human subject remains in hardship and regret.
rows.anchor: لما ختم كلمات الفجر بالجنة التي هي أفضل الأماكن التي يسكنها الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La uqsim affirms the claim while denying its opposite; alternatively, it denies that a truth this evident needs an oath, as in the cited oath over the stars.
rows.anchor: أقسم قسما أثبت مضمونه وأنفي ضده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sacred city is Mecca: difficult to reach, yet increasingly loved; God made it the best land and placed its love in chosen residents and visitors, so it is not called secure in this context of hardship, unlike al-Tin.
rows.anchor: أي الحرام وهو مكة التي لا يصل إليها قاصدوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city is further honored by the Prophet’s presence: ḥill means either his residence or permission for him to do what is forbidden to others, including killing Ibn Khatal after the Hijra; this was foretold in a Meccan sura.
rows.anchor: أي مقيم أو حلال لك ما لم يحل لغيرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the inhabitants treat the Prophet as lawful to harm even though game and trees are protected; repeating ‘this city’ rather than using a pronoun magnifies it and condemns their abuse of believers.
rows.anchor: يستحل أهله منك وأنت أشرف الخلق ما لا يستحلونه من صيد ولا شجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath joins the master of places to the master of people: excellence peaks in each created kind, then in humans, prophets, and Muhammad, the highest rank possible for a creature.
rows.anchor: فقد وقع القسم بسيد البلاد وسيد العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s unsurpassed rank entailed unsurpassed hardship: his people verbally abused him and placed camel entrails on his back while he prostrated, among other persecutions.
rows.anchor: يصبر على أذى قومه بالكلام الذي هو أنفذ من السهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity is enclosed by severe hardship; if left to itself it would perish, and these trials prevent it from claiming divine qualities or union with God.
rows.anchor: أي شدة شديدة ومشقة عظيمة محيطة به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made humans weak despite granting outward and inward faculties to manifest His complete knowledge and power; reason and experience show they pursue evil and cannot choose good without divine enabling.
rows.anchor: مع ما منحه به من القوى الظاهرة والباطنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura’s opening sentence gathers the ideas of all that follows with inimitable concision, while its remaining sentences display miraculous arrangement, structure, linkage, and fit between words and meanings.
rows.anchor: لا قدرة لمخلوق على أن يأتي بجملة واحدة تجمع جميع ما وراءها من الجمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As explained in al-Fajr, worldly ease or restriction does not determine whether a person is honored or humiliated.
rows.anchor: ليستا دائرتين على التنعيم في الدنيا والتضييق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human need for movement and rest, then food and drink, and all their consequences keeps people in continual strain.
rows.anchor: احتياجه أولا إلى مطلق الحركة والسكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first psychological desire is to have everything under one’s control; the fronted ‘against him’ emphasizes the human who imagines nobody can overpower him and defies his Creator.
rows.anchor: أنه يشتهي أن يكون كل من في الوجود في قبضته

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr connects the sura to earlier passages: doomed peoples regret too late, but their fate follows divine decree; hardship tests them and can block those destined for misery from reflection.
rows.anchor: الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr links their claim that nobody can overpower them to divine hardening and cites verses on God’s will to guide or leave people heedless.
rows.anchor: وأغفل قلوبهم فحسبوا أنهم لا يقدر عليهم أحد

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Despite their sight and faculties, people fail to take heed and rescue themselves; if God wills harm for a people, none can avert it.
rows.anchor: فأنت تشاهدهم يا محمد ذوي أبصار وآلات يعتبر بها النظار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Boasting that he spent much wealth suggests the speaker still possesses far more, revealing pride in indebtedness over all people and desire for immeasurable riches.
rows.anchor: فعلم أن مراد الإشارة إلى أن معه أضعاف ما أنفق من حيث إنه حقره بلفظ الإهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two desires are illustrated by a report that Adam’s child would keep wanting gold and by the statement that nothing fills his belly but earth.
rows.anchor: حديث ( لو أن لابن آدم واد من ذهب )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar’s geminated reading of lubad treats it as a plural like rukkaʿ, emphasizing wealth stacked beyond counting or the capacity of the earth.
rows.anchor: جاءت قراءة أبي جعفر بالتشديد على أنه جمع لا بد كركع وراكع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boast presents wealth as a means to impose favors, enslave free people, and command a large following and unquestioned obedience.
rows.anchor: قلدت به أعناق الرجال المنن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited promise of a good life for any believing man or woman means crossing from the low world to a higher realm of pleasure; true freedom is release from desire into obedient service.
rows.anchor: من عمل صالحا من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن فلنحيينه حياة طيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There are two routes: the drawn person is carried by divine attraction, while the seeker struggles with the sword of high aspiration.
rows.anchor: فالمجذوب محمول . والكاسب في تعب المجاهدات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense in ‘What will make you know?’ commonly introduces an explanation of the question, first heightening the obstacle’s difficulty and reward.
rows.anchor: معبرًا بالماضي الذي جرت عادة القرآن بأنه إذا عبر به شرح المستفهم عنه

rows.speaker: البراء
rows.claim: A report from al-Baraʾ distinguishes freeing a person outright from unlocking a neck by contributing toward its price.
rows.anchor: حديث البراء رضي الله عنه ( أعتق النسمة وفك الرقبة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Breaking a neck’s bonds includes freeing someone from captivity, oppression, debt, or illness, as gratitude for God’s favor and love of excellence rather than display or expectation of reward.
rows.anchor: أي من الأسر أو الظلم أو الغرم أو السقم شكرا لمن أولاه الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Feeding on a day of severe hunger means general famine in a hungry place and time; it requires resisting stinginess and fear by trusting God.
rows.anchor: أي جوع عام في مكان جوع وزمان جوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired descriptions use interlocking omission: the orphan is near kin, while the dust-covered poor person is in extreme need; together they imply their opposites and include strangers by stronger reason.
rows.anchor: ذكر القرب أولا يدل على ضده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The orphan’s kinship evokes compassion and the poor person’s dust evokes tenderness; feeding aims only to meet need, and distant orphans and unrelated poor people are included a fortiori.
rows.anchor: وسر ذلك أنه ذكر في اليتيم القرب المعطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding good deeds signal noble character and high aspiration, and sincerity is required for such qualities; thumma introduces a second, later obstacle concerning purified reason.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت هذه الأفعال خيرا في نفسها تدل على جودة الطبع وعلو الهمة وكرم العنصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True believers accepted the caller despite becoming followers after once being followed, reasoning that faith raised them from lowliness toward an exalted rank.
rows.anchor: ولم تحمله حمية الأنف وشماخة النفس على الإباء عن أن يكون تابعا بعد ما كان متبوعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage’s phrase about people of understanding is linked to the cited signs for those endowed with understanding.
rows.anchor: إن في ذلك لآيات لأولي النهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Bakr’s pre-Islamic character included kinship, hospitality, carrying burdens, and helping people facing true calamities; Ibn al-Daghina said such a man should neither leave nor be expelled.
rows.anchor: إن مثلك يا أبا بكر لا يخرج ولا يخرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khadija praised similar virtues in the Prophet after his first encounter with Gabriel, paralleling Abu Bakr’s innate virtues.
rows.anchor: كما قالت خديجة رضي الله عنها للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حين رجع إليها ترجف بوادره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God enabled Abu Bakr to accept the call to Islam immediately and without hesitation.
rows.anchor: توفيقا من الله تعالى لم يتعلثم حين دعاه إلى الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Hudaybiyya Abu Bakr answered Umar with the Prophet’s exact words despite not hearing them beforehand, evidence of his exceptional rank.
rows.anchor: ما قال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سواء حرفا بحرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Bakr never drank wine; when challenged in pagan times, he said he would spend all his wealth on anything that increased his intelligence.
rows.anchor: قال لعشراء : والله لو وجدت شيئا يزيد في عقلي

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said, ‘I entered Islam carrying forward the good I had done’; this validates Abu Bakr’s good deeds from before Islam through his later faith.
rows.anchor: أسلمت على ما سلف منك من خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith elevates a person and leads to religious duties that require the greater struggle against one’s nature; courage is a third virtue, and its hardship is sustained by patience and cooperation.
rows.anchor: وكانت موجبة للجهاد الأكبر من حيث مخالفتها للطبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers mutually counsel patience in demanding acts of duty, including enjoining right even when it may lead to death; bravery is patience for an hour.
rows.anchor: أي صبروا وأوصى بعضهم بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mercy is a fourth obstacle and fruit of patient justice, moderating excess and deficiency; repeating the verb signals that few people practice it, in forms fitting each time and place.
rows.anchor: فكانت الرحمة من ثمرات الاصطبار المثمر للعدالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faithful cultivate mercy through love and aversion for God; faith purifies them from ostentation and self-admiration, making them radiant in knowledge.
rows.anchor: بأن يوطنوا أنفسهم على كل ما يحمل على الرحمة العظيمة التي توجب لهم الحب في الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose of Surat al-Shams is to show God’s control of souls, the lamps of bodies, guiding them to happiness or misery just as He controls the sun and all creation.
rows.anchor: مقصودها إثبات تصرفه سبحانه وتعالى في النفوس التي هي سرج الأبدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura’s name points to its subject through reflection on the oath and what is sworn by.
rows.anchor: واسمها الشمس واضح الدلالة على ذلك بتأمل القسم والمقسم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala names God as supreme king with general control, merciful to all, and especially guiding whom He wills to complete their blessing.
rows.anchor: اللذي خص من شاء بالتوفيق فبنى إنعامه عليهمن على التمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose of Surat al-Shams is to show God’s control of souls, the lamps of bodies, guiding them to happiness or misery just as He controls the sun and all creation.
rows.anchor: مقصودها إثبات تصرفه سبحانه وتعالى في النفوس التي هي سرج الأبدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura’s name points to its subject through reflection on the oath and what is sworn by.
rows.anchor: واسمها الشمس واضح الدلالة على ذلك بتأمل القسم والمقسم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala names God as supreme king with general control, merciful to all, and especially guiding whom He wills to complete their blessing.
rows.anchor: اللذي خص من شاء بالتوفيق فبنى إنعامه عليهمن على التمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura follows the claim that humanity is in hardship and ends with the sealed fire: God is the ultimate agent who turns between a person, heart, and intellect and guides or misguides souls.
rows.anchor: أثبت في سورة البلد أن الإنسان في كبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath begins with the heavenly realm and then souls to establish God’s knowledge, power, necessary existence, and attributes, prompting gratitude as the highest practical perfection.
rows.anchor: فأفاد ذلك قطعا العلم بأنه الفاعل المختار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun brings benefit and harm through light and heat, like intellects that illuminate when sound and become dark when corrupted.
rows.anchor: أي الجامعة بين النفع والضر بالنور والحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍuḥā is the sun’s light from its remarkable body and recalls fires as its power rises; ḍuḥā also means the morning after sunrise, while ḍuḥāʾ means intense heat after a long day.
rows.anchor: المذكر بالنيران إذا أشرقت وقام سلطانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon follows the sun by reflecting its light: proximity dims it, distance increases its illuminated portion to the full moon, then nearness again makes it wane; ‘following’ is a metaphor.
rows.anchor: تبعها في الاستدارة والنور بما دل على أن نوره من نورها من القرب الماحق لنوره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Day is the time for activity and displays the sun in changing conditions; likewise the body may purify or soil the soul and intellect, producing an angelic person when aligned with reason or a devilish one when opposed.
rows.anchor: أي الذي هو محل الانتشار فيما جرت به الأقدار
